title: Round 3 / ECDLP-9: decisive scaling test of the flat-spectrum explanation
question: Do full-range normalized twisted sums X_c for chi(g([k]P)) stay bounded relative to sqrt(p/r) as p grows (Weil-type), with a non-Exp(1) periodogram law, for low-degree g, and approach random-like behaviour for higher-degree g or non-algebraic predicates?
claims: Experimental (toy, p<=1.28e5, 2 seeds): for g=x, x+1, y the full-range |X_c|^2 satisfy max about 4 p/r (does not grow with ln r; slope CI about 0) with 3rd moment 5.0 and KS distance about 0.012 to the Sato-Tate law of (2cos t)^2, supporting a bounded Weil-type behaviour; 2nd moment is 2.00, so the pre-registered rule B (2nd moment != 2) was non-discriminating and the literal verdict is inconclusive.

Experimental: for g=x^2+x+1, x*y, x^3+2 and non-algebraic controls max |X_c|^2 grows like ln r (slope about 0.8-1.7) with real-Gaussian-like 2nd/3rd moments (3, 15); H is refuted for these g at tested sizes. Random +-1 control behaves as Exp(1) (2nd moment 2.0, slope 0.9).
Experimental: no evidence of predicting k mod 2 or k mod 3 from coordinate predicates (bucket 1); no discrete-log leak claimed. Proof status not-applicable/unproved; finite experiments only.
next_action: PI review: decide whether Sato-Tate/SU(2) identification for g in {x,x+1,y} merits a literature check (Katz-type equidistribution for twisted sums) and a proof attempt; test additional g (e.g. 2x, x^2, x^2+1, y+x, higher degrees) and larger p to locate the degree threshold; extend leak sanity to larger moduli. Update HYP-242da418 status.
